II-837CEB8F-159A-4FEE-9A9A-BC7191FEEEBC.title: SERVICE AND GROUNDING EQUIPMENT,  MAIN OVERCURRENT DEVICE, MAIN AND DISTRIBUTION PANELS
II-837CEB8F-159A-4FEE-9A9A-BC7191FEEEBC.helpHtml:
Quick Check:

1. Is the meterbase secure on the wall?

2. Is a drip loop present at weather head?

3. Is the wall anchor in place?

4. Is there a bond wire that connects to the metal plumbing supply lines where supply enters home?

5. Is the Electrical panel missing screws?

6. Do the circuit breaker brands match the panel brand?

7. If the Meterbase is not upgraded but the electrical panel is... Ok, unless the service wire from the meterbase to the panel is upgraded, then the meterbase should have been upgraded also.

8. Is the Meterbase grounded with wire, secure clamp and ground rod?

9. The Main disconnect breaker should be on the outside panel if the inside panel is further than 5 feet from the meterbase.

10. Are there any rusted screws or bus connectors in any panels?

11. Are there any Knockout covers (blanks) missing?

12. Are there any wiring missing romex connectors where wire enters into the panel?

13. Are there any exposed wiring splices outside of the panel or on water heater?

14. Is the panel secure to the wall? Is the Meterbase secure to the wall?

15. Are any panels located too close to water? Hidden inside a cabinet? Not accessible?

More Info:

  1. A bond wire is a ground wire that grounds the panel to the metal plumbing that goes into the soil. A ground wire is the wire outside that goes from the meterbase to the ground rod. In some rural areas or abroad, a bond wire to the metal plumbing is acceptable as the only ground with no ground wire outside. This is on some older homes but not new construction. The problem occurs when the plumber removes the old galvanized metal plumbing and replaces it with plastic or PVC, which removes the only bond/ground wire. We can't depend on the plumber to make sure the electric panel is grounded.
  2. Some electrical contractors say that on some old glass globe meter bases that there is nowhere to put a ground. I have heard some electrical contractors disagree and say that there is always a way to ground the meterbase. So sometimes I write in the report when I see this situation that "there is only one ground wire found on the panel and it leads to a metal plumbing pipe that has been changed to non-metal and there is no ground". Or that it goes to a an older galvanized line that may get changed in the future by a plumber and disconnect the only ground for the panel. I recommend an electrical contractor add another ground wire.
  3. Circuit breaker brand should match the panel. An electrical contractor may point this out to your buyer after they purchase the home. I never used to care about mixed brands as long as they fit properly. But clearly on the label, each panel brand requires their circuit brand only or it will void the UL listing. This was enough to scare my buyer, and I decided that I would not buy any more breakers. Since then, I've discovered that some electrical contractors feel that some brands can mix because of companies merging. I disagree unless those names are also on that particular panel label. SIEMENS, ITE and GOULD supposedly are one company. MURRAY may also be a part of SIEMENS.
  4. WESTINGHOUSE, BRYANT AND CUTLER-HAMMER are supposedly one company.
  5. Remember: The electrical panel has a label on it. And somewhere it usually states that only their brand is allowed to be used. All other brands will void warranty or may be a hazard.
  6. General Switch Brand panel may allow other brands that will fit. If they do, they will indicate it on the label.
  7. When in doubt, recommend an electrical contractor. If a fire was to occur and later it was found that the source was from the panel and it had different breakers, the homeowner would not be denied the insurance claim. But, the insurance company may feel that the recent inspection should have revealed it. Especially when a UL label on the panel states that no other brand is allowed.
  8. The insurance company may seek compensation from the inspector in the form of litigation. Whether they do or don't, right is right and wrong is wrong, so I mention it.
  9. There should also be a ground wire attached to a driven ground rod at the meter base. This grounds the panel itself.
  10. Some local electrical contractors may say that one is really good enough (at plumbing or meter base). But that's true only if the supply lines are not metal (Pex, CPVC etc.). If only the metal plumbing has a ground and not the meter base, and the metal plumbing is old corroded galvanized piping that gets replaced with Pex, there would then be no ground.
  11. Or, if the plumber replaced the old piping with copper or metal, it would be up to him to reset the ground and clamp onto the new pipe. And we all know plumbers aren't electrical contractors.

Reference Materials:

II-840A9AE5-0D06-4D6D-8185-C70E9DFE9C8A.title: BRANCH CIRCUITS-CONNECTED DEVICES AND FIXTURES (Report as in need of repair the lack of ground fault circuit protection where required.)
II-840A9AE5-0D06-4D6D-8185-C70E9DFE9C8A.helpHtml: Use this question for miscellaneous electrical items found (i.e. loose splices, boxes missing cover plates etc). GFCI OUTLETS: I use a simple three-prong plug with a GFCI test button. It of course identifies whether or not the outlet is grounded, and if the polarity is correct. Some tips are: Your three-prong GFCI test plug will not"Trip" the outlet if it is a non-grounded GFCI. But it still should trip by pressing the test button on outlet, and kill the circuit. A Non-grounded outlet can be corrected by either attaching a ground wire to the outlet and attach to a metal rod or metal plumbing pipe. Or replace three-prong non-grounded outlet with a three-prong GFCI outlet. A sticker should be on the outlet that identifies it as non-grounded. Or last, change the circuit breaker to a GFCI breaker at panel. You can "Trip" a Non-grounded GFCI with a voltmeter by placing one prong of the voltmeter in the short slit of the outlet, and take the other prong of the voltmeter and touch a metal plumbing pipe (that eventually contacts the soil). Most three-prong GFCI plugs will show two lights at end of plug when outlet being tested is grounded. When you press the button on the plug, The two lights should remain lit and strong. If however, the plug lights up one of the two grounding lights "Faint or Dim" and you press the button on the plug and it shows "Reverse polarity," it may just be a "loose" ground wire and can be corrected a lot easier than having to install a ground wire. Another tip is "Just because you can press the test button on the GFCI outlet using your finger and it "Trips," doesn't mean it "Killed the circuit." It could be defective.  New GFCI outlets that are installed can be defective. Always use the three-prong GFCI test plug on every three-prong outlet. HOMEOWNERS frequently use a Freezer in their garage. And most outlets in garage are on a GFCI Circuit. When you're inspecting the home, DON'T FORGET TO RE-SET THE GFCI OUTLET, OR YOU MAY BE BUYING THEIR SPOILED FOOD!

II-87449E32-A027-4D1B-9D6B-539DF2531EFB.title: GARAGE DOOR (S)
II-87449E32-A027-4D1B-9D6B-539DF2531EFB.helpHtml:
Quick Check:

1. Is there any staining or discoloration that warrants a finger pressure test on exterior door trim /jambs at bottom ?

2. Does the garage door opening height and width seem normal?

3. The garage door must reverse when met with resistance regardless of whether or not they have sensors. Sensors should be no higher off the floor than 6" or according to manufacturer specs.

4. What is the condition of the weather-stripping at garage door floor and sides?

5. Check both sides of Garage door for damage?

6. The "jerk and let go" test for the garage door works best but there is a risk of damaging the door if you don't let go quick enough. A 2 x 4 block placed on floor can damage a metal door if door does not reverse (not recommended).

8. Note older garage door springs that do not have retention cables to contain the spring if the cable breaks.

More Info:

  1. Always open and shut a door from both sides and note whether or not the door latches.
  2. Also note if the door is out of square enough that it no longer ensures privacy.
  3. Check for holes in doors and for a doorstop on each one. Note any trim or hardware missing (check all doors).
  4. Basement or Crawlspace: Make sure that the door fits properly and is properly painted. Look at the ground in front of the door for negative slope that may allow water intrusion.
  5. Check to see if the door is delaminating or deteriorated at the bottom .
  6. Sliding glass and patio doors: Open and close doors as needed and check for "daylight" and continuous weather-stripping.
  7. Also, close the door with knob until it latches. Then turn deadbolt and check strike for proper alignment and a tight fit.
  8. Also look carefully at the glass, and check for "Cloudy" appearance or cracked glass. This is a good time to inspect the floor area around door for possible water intrusion or deterioration.
  9. Garage doors: Raise the garage door and lay a 2 x 4 block on the floor at the middle of the door opening (except a metal door that could be damaged by a 2 x 4 block). Document if the door reverses or not.
  10. If you use your hand to provide resistance and the door does not reverse, you can severely damage the door if you're not careful. The door can "fold-up" damaging the door panel and chain drive.
  11. Even if the door has electronic sensors, it still should reverse when met with resistance. Adjustment screws are usually found on the side and rear of opener. These door adjustment screws can be tricky to adjust.

II-8C277517-CFDB-401B-936E-ABB26D125DCB.title: POLARITY AND GROUNDING OF RECEPTACLES WITHIN 6 FEET OF INTERIOR PLUMBING FIXTURES, AND ALL RECEPTACLES IN GARAGE, CARPORT,  EXTERIOR WALLS OF INSPECTED STRUCTURE
II-8C277517-CFDB-401B-936E-ABB26D125DCB.helpHtml:
Quick Check:

1. Do you notice any GFCI outlets with freezers plugged into them? Don't forget to reset GFCI. Two prong plugs in the Garage or around any areas with water?

More Info:

  1. I use a simple three-prong plug with a GFCI test button. It identifies whether or not the outlet is grounded, and if the polarity is correct.
  2. Some tips are: Your three-prong GFCI test plug will not "trip" the outlet if it is a non-grounded GFCI. But it still should trip by pressing the test button on outlet, and kill the circuit.
  3. A non-grounded outlet can be corrected by either attaching a ground wire to the outlet and attach it to a metal rod or a metal plumbing pipe.
  4. Or, replace the three-prongnon-grounded outlet with a three-prong GFCI outlet. A sticker should be on the outlet that identifies it as non-grounded.
  5. Or last, change the circuit breaker to a GFCI breaker at the panel.
  6. You can "trip" a non-grounded GFCI with a voltmeter by placing one prong of the voltmeter in the short slit of the outlet, and take the other prong of the voltmeter and touch a metal plumbing pipe (that eventually contacts the soil).
  7. Most three-prong GFCI plugs will show two lights at the end of the plug when the outlet being tested is grounded. When you press the button on the plug, both lights should remain lit and strong. If however, the plug lights up only one of the two grounding lights "Faint or Dim" and you press the button on the plug and it shows "Reverse polarity", it may just be a "loose" ground wire and can be corrected a lot easier than having to install a new ground wire.
  8. Just because you can press the test button on the GFCI outlet using your finger and it "trips," doesn't mean it killed the circuit. It could be defective.
  9. New GFCI outlets can be defective when installed.
  10. Always use the three-prong GFCI test plug on every three-prong outlet.
  11. Homeowners frequently use a freezer in their garage. Most outlets in the garage are on a GFCI Circuit. When you're inspecting the building don't forget to reset the GFCI outlet or you may be buying the homeowners spoiled food.

Reference Materials:

II-8F7A2745-775E-4A77-95C3-A761ABEF071E.title: SEWER SCOPE INSPECTION
II-8F7A2745-775E-4A77-95C3-A761ABEF071E.helpHtml:
Quick Check:

1. Is the sump pump in a proper container?

2. Does the drain for the sump pump exit the home?

3. Is there a proper GFCI outlet provided?

4. The sump pump must not be using an extension cord or temporary wiring.

More Info:

  1. Sump pumps work fine when all the water is removed and air dries out the crawlspace within 2-3 days. If all the water is not removed, then the pump is not adequate and more corrective action is needed.
  2. When recommending a sump pump be installed, you should think about trenches around the perimeter with gravel installed leading to the lowest area and a way to exit water from home without using the sewer system, so our taxpayer dollars don't treat the rain water.
  3. Think about electricity which usually requires an electrical contractor to install a GFCI outlet within reach of the sump pump cord (no extension cords).
  4. Don't forget the plastic vapor barrier. If all that makes sense then it may solve a water problem. Another problem to look for is an approved sump pump container, not a bucket. What's the difference? A lot of difference, if a water infiltration expert comes behind you slinging mud. A bucket with a few drain holes in the bottom should work - but I would reference in my report that the bucket while appears to work fine is not an approved sump pump container as some repair specialist may note.
  5. Don't forget to raise the rod and float to see if it actually works.

Reference Materials:

II-913F7A90-9E7B-4E61-A872-E1516EDDD0C4.title: WINDOWS (REPRESENTATIVE NUMBER)
II-913F7A90-9E7B-4E61-A872-E1516EDDD0C4.helpHtml:
Quick Check:

1. Did you test the windows or write "Not Inspected" when a window has knick-knacks stacked on it?

2. Be sure to note if a window A/C is preventing testing the operation of a window.

3. Are storm windows missing or damaged on single pane windows?

4. Is any weatherstripping missing on windows?

5. Are sash cords missing or replaced with jamb hardware on the windows?

6. Was every accessible window tested for operation? If not, did you note which ones were not tested?

7. Cloudy windows? Note windows that appear cloudy and also note windows that are out of reach and can't be determined if they are cloudy or just dirty.

More Info:

  1. This is where you look for cloudy windows and lock hardware and cracked or loose glass.
  2. Also check the sill for strength against deterioration.
  3. Walls leaking around windows can sometimes be discovered by inspecting the sill for deterioration.

II-9689781F-AD9F-497F-B9A7-4B8F9AEEC052.title: POLARITY AND GROUNDING OF RECEPTACLES
II-9689781F-AD9F-497F-B9A7-4B8F9AEEC052.helpHtml:
Quick Check:

1. Do you notice any GFCI outlets with freezers plugged into them? Don't forget to reset GFCI. Two prong plugs in the Garage or around any areas with water?

More Info:

  1. I use a simple three-prong plug with a GFCI test button. It identifies whether or not the outlet is grounded, and if the polarity is correct.
  2. Some tips are: Your three-prong GFCI test plug will not "trip" the outlet if it is a non-grounded GFCI. But it still should trip by pressing the test button on outlet, and kill the circuit.
  3. A non-grounded outlet can be corrected by either attaching a ground wire to the outlet and attach it to a metal rod or a metal plumbing pipe.
  4. Or, replace the three-prongnon-grounded outlet with a three-prong GFCI outlet. A sticker should be on the outlet that identifies it as non-grounded.
  5. Or last, change the circuit breaker to a GFCI breaker at the panel.
  6. You can "trip" a non-grounded GFCI with a voltmeter by placing one prong of the voltmeter in the short slit of the outlet, and take the other prong of the voltmeter and touch a metal plumbing pipe (that eventually contacts the soil).
  7. Most three-prong GFCI plugs will show two lights at the end of the plug when the outlet being tested is grounded. When you press the button on the plug, both lights should remain lit and strong. If however, the plug lights up only one of the two grounding lights "Faint or Dim" and you press the button on the plug and it shows "Reverse polarity", it may just be a "loose" ground wire and can be corrected a lot easier than having to install a new ground wire.
  8. Just because you can press the test button on the GFCI outlet using your finger and it "trips," doesn't mean it killed the circuit. It could be defective.
  9. New GFCI outlets can be defective when installed.
  10. Always use the three-prong GFCI test plug on every three-prong outlet.
  11. Homeowners frequently use a freezer in their garage. Most outlets in the garage are on a GFCI Circuit. When you're inspecting the home don't forget to reset the GFCI outlet or you may be buying the homeowners spoiled food.

II-9DE8D8BB-D5EB-4794-B24F-89DF8E216857.title: DISHWASHER
II-9DE8D8BB-D5EB-4794-B24F-89DF8E216857.helpHtml: The first thing you should do when you begin an inspection is start dishwasher to allow time to complete cycle before you through. Examine the dishwasher, drain line and run dishwasher through a cycle. If they're dirty dishes inside, add detergent (usually stored under the sink). Just make sure its detergent for dishwasher and not dishwashing detergent, or you'll be there for a while. Check all the movable parts and the heating element and support clips. Make sure the unit is securely mounted to countertop. Remember a leaky gasket could result in a new dishwasher, so always run through a cycle to check for leaks.

II-A04796F8-A58B-41AD-9D13-58524B0BD935.title: SEWER SCOPE INSPECTION
II-A04796F8-A58B-41AD-9D13-58524B0BD935.helpHtml:
Quick Check:

1. Is the sump pump in a proper container?

2. Does the drain for the sump pump exit the home?

3. Is there a proper GFCI outlet provided?

4. The sump pump must not be using an extension cord or temporary wiring.

More Info:

  1. Sump pumps work fine when all the water is removed and air dries out the crawlspace within 2-3 days. If all the water is not removed, then the pump is not adequate and more corrective action is needed.
  2. When recommending a sump pump be installed, you should think about trenches around the perimeter with gravel installed leading to the lowest area and a way to exit water from home without using the sewer system, so our taxpayer dollars don't treat the rain water.
  3. Think about electricity which usually requires an electrical contractor to install a GFCI outlet within reach of the sump pump cord (no extension cords).
  4. Don't forget the plastic vapor barrier. If all that makes sense then it may solve a water problem. Another problem to look for is an approved sump pump container, not a bucket. What's the difference? A lot of difference, if a water infiltration expert comes behind you slinging mud. A bucket with a few drain holes in the bottom should work - but I would reference in my report that the bucket while appears to work fine is not an approved sump pump container as some repair specialist may note.
  5. Don't forget to raise the rod and float to see if it actually works.

II-A730B342-B3E9-420C-9613-309F0ABAE845.title: HOT WATER SYSTEMS, CONTROLS, CHIMNEYS, FLUES AND VENTS
II-A730B342-B3E9-420C-9613-309F0ABAE845.helpHtml:
Quick Check:

1. Is the gas water heater 18" off the floor and mounted on a proper stand or support?

2. Is the water heater strapped securely to the wall (required in earthquake zones)?

3. If the gas line to the water heater or furnace could be bumped or ruptured by a vehicle, a pole or guard post should be recommended

4. If the water heater is in the crawlspace or basement, it should not be lower than ground level. You may not dig a hole to set the water heater in.

5. Use a lighter at the draft hood when the gas water heater is on to check for proper draw.

6. A gas water heater in the closet needs fresh air from the attic at the ceiling and near the floor.

More Info:

  1. Inspect the plumbing connections and tank housing.
  2. Note rust signs from moisture or condensation (if in a damp area of building) or possible leak at the liner.
  3. Rust along the bottom can be caused when water leaks out while changing heating elements. Sometimes it's hard to distinguish. If you discover rust along the bottom, then remove panel access and feel the insulation to determine if it's currently wet.
  4. Water heaters installed in a crawlspace should not be below ground level.
  5. Gas water heaters installed in a garage should be at least 18 inches off the ground.
  6. When two gas vent pipes enter the chimney together, the highest BTU should enter chimney under the smaller BTU.
  7. Gas water heaters should have the thermostat turned up to force it to come on in order to test the draw at the diverter with a match or lighter. If the draw does not noticeably suck in flame on a match, there could be a venting problem.
  8. White deposits and rust on metal vent pipe can occur from moisture in the gas when not venting properly.
  9. A greasy residue on top of the gas water heater is also a sign of a vent problem.
  10. A blackened or smoky appearance on and around the housing near the flame of a gas water heater indicates the need for more air (combustion air).
  11. The T&P valve (Test and Pressure or Pop off valve) can look fine if the building has not had the water heater on 24 hours before inspection. It can then leak after the buyer moves in. The primary reason is that pressure on the system builds up at night when no one is using water. With gas, the added pressure is a result of steam. Be aware of this when you inspect a vacant building and the water heater has not been on for 24 hours prior.

II-A88E3312-1E11-4490-A390-603AB4053517.title: INTERIOR DRAIN, WASTE AND VENT SYSTEMS
II-A88E3312-1E11-4490-A390-603AB4053517.helpHtml:
Quick Check:

1.(New home) Did you fill sink basins full of water and drain simultaneously to check for leaks at the basket strainer or waster line connections?

2.(Sinks) Is the waste line a P-trap? Is is vented? Are there shut-off valves under the sink?

3. Did you pull back insulation under the bathroom floors to check for leaks or deterioration?

4. Note any temporary repairs to waste lines which include caulking, putty, or homeowner repairs using clamps or flexible piping.

5. Rusted metal waste lines can sometimes collapse or fail upon touching them during inspection.

6. If the washing machine drain line is 1 1/2 inch (older), instead of 2 inch then note the possibility that newer washing machines may overflow a smaller drain (2 inch diameter recommended).

More Info:

  1. Make sure the waste line for plumbing has a trap and vent.
  2. Many older homes still have a 1 1/2" diameter waste line and new washing machines have stronger pumps that may overflow the drain. Not all but some. Look for signs on the wall or floor, or the drain hose may have been modified in some way.
  3. "Gray water" is a term that means that the water drains into the yard and not the sewer or septic system. This could be a violation in your area. Consult with the health department or building safety department on this issue.
  4. Some septic tanks were not designed for the volume of water from a washing machine and could clog if gray water was connected to it. If you discover gray water use, note the possibilities.
  5. The outlet for the washing machine should be grounded. A repair would be to install a GFCI outlet.
  6. Old cast iron waste lines often ooze a leak at pipe connections because the old seals in between pipe connections are deteriorating. It will still work but may need repair. Plumbers who repair these old pipes do not like to repair only one connection, because working on these old pipes can cause other joint connections nearby to fail (hammering, vibration etc.). They will sometimes explain the cost and that it usually includes a larger section for replacement.
  7. The crud that builds up on the inside of these pipes is surprising. That's why sometimes a home plumbing system could work fine until left vacant for 3 -6 months and then the crud inside the pipes begin to dry and fall down and clog pipes. Same is true for old galvanized supply lines when left vacant for long periods. Not always the case but more often than you would think.

Reference Materials:

II-A971769E-CD55-466C-86EB-8D42DCDED315.title: DISTRIBUTION SYSTEMS (including fans, pumps, ducts and piping, with supports, insulation, air filters, registers, radiators, fan coil units and convectors)
II-A971769E-CD55-466C-86EB-8D42DCDED315.helpHtml:
Quick Check:

1. Inspect filter condition and look for a good seal around the filter door or compartment?

2. Is there damaged or loose ductwork, duct tape?

3. Does the furnace or airhandler shut off when the blower door is removed (safety switch)?

More Info:

  1. Make sure you note if a room does not have a register or vent.
  2. Also inspect all ductwork accessible. Note if the ductwork is not insulated if there is AC.
  3. Many times the tape is failing and the ductpipe has pulled loose from the register underneath the floor.
  4. Pull out or examine the filter as part of your air handler inspection. Many times the filter is the wrong size or clogged beyond belief.
  5. A clogged filter can cause $10 a month in electricity costs and shorten the life of the unit not to mention the poor air quality.
  6. New construction: Make sure you try to look deep inside the return air cavity in the wall to look for unhealthy items left behind by sub contractors.
  7. Radiators for old boilers can clog or not heat fully. Sometimes they can be blown clean by a boiler technician and sometimes they cannot. One radiator could cost $1000 or more easily ($80 a rung so I've heard) so be sure and write up any that do not get hot on both ends as needing servicing or further inspection by a Boiler technician.
  8. Read the auto-comments in the heat section.

II-AC44894D-840B-4987-809C-A92A93D15CEF.title: HEATING EQUIPMENT
II-AC44894D-840B-4987-809C-A92A93D15CEF.helpHtml:
Quick Check:

1. Is the heat pump / condenser level?

2. Are the foam sleeves on the suction line intact?

3. Are bushes or a fence obstructing air flow?

4. Hydronic systems should have a water heater that is designed for heating the home and not use converted water heaters. Converted water heaters may not have a high enough BTU rating.

5. Are there any electric outlets located on the wall above the electric baseboard which could be a possible fire hazard?

More Info:

  1. Heating Equipment over 15 years old and still operating should still be noted as old, and recommend servicing them annually to monitor for safe operation.
  2. (Oil furnaces) Check around the sight hole for smoke stains around the collar that may be leaking fumes.
  3. Examine the vent pipe and where it enters chimney for integrity and proper seal.
  4. Check for back drafting by using a lighter or match around joints in the vent pipe, or at an existing test hole (if any).
  5. An erratic movement of the damper lid on the vent pipe and/or soot build-up should be noted.
  6. The furnace should run for at least 15 minutes.
  7. It's a good technique to observe the firing, or ignition, of the furnace. To do this, use the cut-off switch at the furnace before you set the thermostat to turn the furnace on. If it's not running normally, recommend a licensed heat contractor for service and repair as needed.
  8. Learn how to perform a smoke bomb test. Use a Gas Tracer.
  9. ( GAS FURNACES ) Use a gas tracer around the unit. Examine burners and raceway for charred bits and recommend service if bits are excessive or flame is not even.
  10. If flame dances sharply or rolls under the burner recommend service.
  11. Heat exchangers or the steel liner is more likely to crack near the pilot light.
  12. ( BOILERS ) should be tested for 30 to 45 minutes to allow all radiators to heat fully. Some radiators that are old may take longer to heat but you have to decide while your there if they heat from one end to the other. This time is needed to allow pressure to build and check for leaks. Radiators are extremely expensive and you don't want to miss even one. If over 15 years old and operating well it should be noted as old and recommend servicing annually to monitor for safe operation.
  13. Check around the sight hole for smoke stains around the collar that may be leaking fumes. Examine the vent pipe and where it enters the chimney for integrity and proper seal.
  14. Check for back drafting by using a lighter or match around joints in the vent pipe, or at an existing test hole (if any).
  15. Steam boilers have a sight glass to check water level.
  16. Circulating boilers do not have a sight glass.
  17. Boilers should be flushed regularly as part of a normal maintenance schedule.
  18. ( HEAT PUMPS ) should not be ran in AC mode if temp outside is @ 65 degrees or less. You could damage the unit.
  19. Be sure and note if you did not inspect it. Just because you have heat coming out of the registers doesn't mean your compressor outside is working.
  20. The fan outside should be moving. Just because the fan outside is moving doesn't mean you have heat.
  21. Grab the suction line before it enters air handler inside and feel for heat.
  22. In summer, hand check the suction line for ice cold. No cold feeling means recommending service.
  23. The coils inside the air handler may need cleaning or the liquid line may need refrigerant.
  24. Only trouble shooting by a qualified heat contractor can determine exactly.
  25. The ambient air test differential on a heat pump should be between 14 and 22 degrees. Use a thermometer at the main plenum and use one at the return air at the air handler. The difference in these (in AC mode) should be 14 to 22 degrees.
  26. ( ELECTRIC BASE ) should be turned on and checked for proper operation, securely fastened to wall or floor.
  27. There should never be an outlet on the wall directly above electric base.
  28. Remove the front cover on the baseboard and inspect the wire that runs the length of the base located inside a tube. This wire can become brittle or weak over time, and cause abnormal heating up of unit and can cause a fire.

II-AC5EE73E-99FD-4899-93FB-73E93929CC83.title: COOLING AND AIR HANDLER EQUIPMENT
II-AC5EE73E-99FD-4899-93FB-73E93929CC83.helpHtml:

2. Are the foam sleeves on the suction line intact?

The home inspector is not required to:Operate cooling systems when weather conditions or other circumstances may cause equipment damage; Observe non-central air conditioners; or Observe the uniformity or adequacy of cool-air supply to the various rooms. Ambient air test is when you stick two meat thermometers into the main plenum of the air handler. One in the return air and one in the supply. Preferably near each other at the main trunk. If the AC has been running for an adequate amount of time before test you should see a range somewhere between 14 and 22 degrees. The supply should be the colder of the two. This test is not conclusive because of varying conditions but if it's out of range and the AC has had time to cool the home, then you can recommend an HVAC person (Heating Ventilation and Air Conditioning)

II-AF5ED8C0-C2CA-43FF-A57A-0DB8C5A75CEA.helpHtml:
Quick Check:

More Info:

  1. Don't miss the absence of a vent in a room or you could be sued and be liable for the cost to put one in.
  2. One must also consider: Why isn't one there? It could be the size of the heat/AC unit which would require a bigger unit or perhaps there is no physical way to install one. Extreme remodeling may be involved.
  3. Also, stay alert for the type of heating system in the house with an AC condenser. If it's boiler heat and there is an AC unit outside, and the house is 2 story, it is likely that the AC serves the upstairs only. Therefore it is necessary to point this out in your report.

II-B16E884F-DC63-4741-9B5E-C4B3978D871F.title: GARAGE CEILINGS
II-B16E884F-DC63-4741-9B5E-C4B3978D871F.helpHtml:
Quick Check:

1. Be sure to note any ceiling, or projection from a ceiling, in any finished room that is lower than 7 feet from the floor.

More Info:

  1. Look at an old home with an old eye.
  2. Always note water stains
  3. On newer homes, note nail pops, exposed or loose sheetrock tape and repair signs.
  4. Workmanship is important on all homes, but especially new ones.
  5. Look for signs of only one coat of paint, poor sanding, nail indentations etc.
  6. Look at the perimeter of the floor for water stains or deterioration.

Reference Materials:

The home inspector shall observe: Walls, ceiling, and floors; Steps, stairways, balconies, and railings; Counters and a representative number of cabinets; and A representative number of doors and windows. The home inspector shall: Operate a representative number of windows and interior doors; and Report signs of abnormal or harmful water penetration into the building or signs of abnormal or harmful condensation on building components.

The home inspector is not required to observe: Paint, wallpaper, and other finish treatments on the interior walls, ceilings, and floors; Carpeting; or Draperies, blinds, or other window treatments.

II-B1DBC8DD-6268-483D-83E9-199BBC3F4376.title: VAPOR RETARDERS (ON GROUND IN CRAWLSPACE OR BASEMENT)
II-B1DBC8DD-6268-483D-83E9-199BBC3F4376.helpHtml:
Quick Check:

1. Is there a vapor barrier (6 mil recommended) on dirt floor of basement or crawlspace?

2.. Foundation vents should have screens.

More Info:

  1. To get R-Value for Fiberglass, Rock Wool and Mineral Fiber, multiply the thickness in inches by 3.142857.
  2. For Cellulose, multiply inches by 3.6666 to find R-Value.
  3. Insulation usually comes in four types: Loose-fill, Batts, Rolls and Rigid Foam Board.
  4. Fiberglass is recycled glass and sand
  5. Rock Wool is recycled Steel scraps and Basaltic Rock
  6. Cellulose is recycled newspapers treated with fire retardant chemicals (Borax).
  7. Rigid Foam Board (used on exterior side of walls and behind the ceiling panel of a Cathedral ceiling) obviously not visible or accessible during an inspection.
  8. A home can lose 50% of it's heat through the roof, with 25% going through the walls and windows, and 25% through the floor.

A rough guess of R value in the attic is determined by the thickness of insulation:

  1. about 6 inches thick or just under 22 R value
  2. about 7 inches thick or 25.6 R-value
  3. about 8 inches thick or just over 29 R-value
  4. about 9 inches thick or just under 33 R-value
  5. about 10 inches thick or just over 36.6 R-value
  6. about 11 inches thick or just over 40 R-value
  7. about 12 inches thick or just under 44 R-value
  8. about 13 inches thick or 47.6 R-value
  9. about 14 inches thick or just at 51 R-value
  10. about 15 inches thick or just under 55 R-value
  11. about 16 inches thick or 58 R-value

Floor spaces:

A vapor barrier is a roll of plastic (6 mil thick preferred) that is spread out over the crawlspace to keep moisture from entering the crawlspace from the ground. It is essential and inexpensive compared to its prevention abilities.

Reference Materials:

The home inspector shall observe: Insulation and vapor retarders in unfinished spaces; Ventilation of attics and foundation areas; Kitchen, bathroom, and laundry venting systems; and the operation of any readily accessible attic ventilation fan, and, when temperature permits, the operation of any readily accessible thermostatic control. The home inspector shall describe: Insulation in unfinished spaces; and Absence of insulation in unfinished space at conditioned surfaces. The home inspector shall: Move insulation where readily visible evidence indicates the need to do so; and Move insulation where chimneys penetrate roofs, where plumbing drain/waste pipes penetrate floors, adjacent to earth filled stoops or porches, and at exterior doors.

The home inspector is not required to report on: Concealed insulation and vapor retarders; or Venting equipment that is integral with household appliances.

II-B1EA8FC2-D640-4F91-8C5F-0F292323AD06.helpHtml:
Quick Check:

  2. One must also consider: Why isn't one there? It could be the size of the heat/AC unit which would require a bigger unit or perhaps there is no physical way to install one. Extreme remodeling may be involved.

II-B39E4A14-4620-48F2-96DD-938880523B8A.title: HOT WATER SYSTEMS, CONTROLS, CHIMNEYS, FLUES AND VENTS
II-B39E4A14-4620-48F2-96DD-938880523B8A.helpHtml:
Quick Check:

1. Is the gas water heater 18" off the floor and mounted on a proper stand or support?

2. Is the water heater strapped securely to the wall (required in earthquake zones)?

3. If the gas line to the water heater or furnace could be bumped or ruptured by a vehicle, a pole or guard post should be recommended

4. If the water heater is in the crawlspace or basement, it should not be lower than ground level. You may not dig a hole to set the water heater in.

5. Use a lighter at the draft hood when the gas water heater is on to check for proper draw.

6. A gas water heater in the closet needs fresh air from the attic at the ceiling and near the floor.

More Info:

  1. Inspect the plumbing connections and tank housing.
  2. Note rust signs from moisture or condensation (if in a damp area of home) or possible leak at the liner.
  3. Rust along the bottom can be caused when water leaks out while changing heating elements. Sometimes it's hard to distinguish. If you discover rust along the bottom, then remove panel access and feel the insulation to determine if it's currently wet.
  4. Water heaters installed in a crawlspace should not be below ground level.
  5. Gas water heaters installed in a garage should be at least 18 inches off the ground.
  6. When two gas vent pipes enter the chimney together, the highest BTU should enter chimney under the smaller BTU.
  7. Gas water heaters should have the thermostat turned up to force it to come on in order to test the draw at the diverter with a match or lighter. If the draw does not noticeably suck in flame on a match, there could be a venting problem.
  8. White deposits and rust on metal vent pipe can occur from moisture in the gas when not venting properly.
  9. A greasy residue on top of the gas water heater is also a sign of a vent problem.
  10. A blackened or smoky appearance on and around the housing near the flame of a gas water heater indicates the need for more air (combustion air).
  11. The T&P valve (Test and Pressure or Pop off valve) can look fine if the home has not had the water heater on 24 hours before inspection. It can then leak after the buyer moves in. The primary reason is that pressure on the system builds up at night when no one is using water. With gas, the added pressure is a result of steam. Be aware of this when you inspect a vacant home and the water heater has not been on for 24 hours prior.

Reference Materials:

II-B3C09C0C-6577-413B-A786-BEAEC3C6BC71.title: CHIMNEYS, FLUES AND VENTS (for fireplaces, gas water heaters or heat systems)
II-B3C09C0C-6577-413B-A786-BEAEC3C6BC71.helpHtml:
Quick Check:

1. Is there any gas venting that exits home too close to the gas meter, a window or under a deck?

2. Is the chimney leaning or are there signs of trim rework where the chimney contacts the wall of the home?

3. When the gas furnace and gas water heater connect to one vent, the highest BTU unit needs to connect on the bottom.

4. In most areas, the liners for wood burning stoves or fireplaces cannot share the liner with other fuel burning type units such as Gas.

5. Unless you can clearly see all of the liner from end to end, use the auto-comment that the chimney liner was not inspected

6. Examine the vent pipe that connects furnace to chimney for rust or white deposits

More Info:

  1. Usually 1/4 inch or more of creosote should tell you to recommend cleaning.
  2. A chimney fire can sometimes occur on clay liners with no consequence if water was not poured on it from the fire department.
  3. Water can crack the liner. Fire can burn at 2000 degrees and a metal liner for a fireplace that has had a chimney fire, or became to hot, will have a rainbow color outside above the roof on the shiny metal vent pipe. The metal liner is safe for one chimney fire but not two. If you see this rainbow color, I would recommend a chimney sweep inspect it to determine if a chimney fire occurred and if this liner is safe to use.
  4. Woodstove inserts must have a flue connector that connects the insert to its liner. If not, creosote can collect on top of the insert (a wheel barrow load) and cause a chimney fire that can destroy a brick chimney - if not the home. Even if you cannot determine if a liner connecting the insert to the chimney liner exists, you should write up that it cannot be determined.

Reference Materials:

II-B72A3956-10CB-4CAC-8849-03AAA4923837.title: WALLS
II-B72A3956-10CB-4CAC-8849-03AAA4923837.helpHtml:
Quick Check:

1. Check for firewall separation when the garage wall is integral with another unit/condo.

2. Do you have a clear view to inspect all areas in the Garage?

3. Check the garage wall for vehicle damage or material knocked loose at the soleplate.

4. Check the wall behind the refrigerator for mold?

(Bath)

5. Did you knock on the wall tile at the bath surround to check for loose tile?

6. Did you note loose or missing grout?

7. Is there improper caulk instead of grout and seal?

8. Are there loose, damaged or missing wall accessories such as a towel bar, etc?

9. Is the grab bar inside the tub surround loose?

10. Look for bowed paneling in the lower level or basement, which would be typical of a room with higher moisture levels than the rest of building.

More Info:

  1. Black flash marks on or around an outlet on the wall should be noted.
  2. Understand the difficulties of removing old wall paper.
  3. Note areas where there are bedded nails, and seams where they were not sanded down smooth before painting.
  4. Understand that some walls have oil based paint on them andall buyers are planning to use latex which means their paint job will fail.
  5. Oil can go over oil based or latex. Latex cannot go over oil based paint.
  6. There is a product that is a sealer/primer that would need to go over oil based paint and then latex can be applied.

Reference Materials:

II-B7A2A8B3-417E-493D-A45B-9C242A16CC3D.title: PLUMBING  DRAIN, WASTE AND VENT SYSTEMS IN THIS UNIT
II-B7A2A8B3-417E-493D-A45B-9C242A16CC3D.helpHtml:
Quick Check:

1.(New building) Did you fill sink basins full of water and drain simultaneously to check for leaks at the basket strainer or waster line connections?

2.(Sinks) Is the waste line a P-trap? Is is vented? Are there shut-off valves under the sink?

3. Did you pull back insulation under the bathroom floors to check for leaks or deterioration?

4. Note any temporary repairs to waste lines which include caulking, putty, or homeowner repairs using clamps or flexible piping.

5. Rusted metal waste lines can sometimes collapse or fail upon touching them during inspection.

6. If the washing machine drain line is 1 1/2 inch (older), instead of 2 inch then note the possibility that newer washing machines may overflow a smaller drain (2 inch diameter recommended).

More Info:

  1. Make sure the waste line for plumbing has a trap and vent.
  2. Many older homes still have a 1 1/2" diameter waste line and new washing machines have stronger pumps that may overflow the drain. Not all but some. Look for signs on the wall or floor, or the drain hose may have been modified in some way.
  3. "Gray water" is a term that means that the water drains into the yard and not the sewer or septic system. This could be a violation in your area. Consult with the health department or building safety department on this issue.
  4. Some septic tanks were not designed for the volume of water from a washing machine and could clog if gray water was connected to it. If you discover gray water use, note the possibilities.
  5. The outlet for the washing machine should be grounded. A repair would be to install a GFCI outlet.
  6. Old cast iron waste lines often ooze a leak at pipe connections because the old seals in between pipe connections are deteriorating. It will still work but may need repair. Plumbers who repair these old pipes do not like to repair only one connection, because working on these old pipes can cause other joint connections nearby to fail (hammering, vibration etc.). They will sometimes explain the cost and that it usually includes a larger section for replacement.
  7. The crud that builds up on the inside of these pipes is surprising. That's why sometimes a building plumbing system could work fine until left vacant for 3 -6 months and then the crud inside the pipes begin to dry and fall down and clog pipes. Same is true for old galvanized supply lines when left vacant for long periods. Not always the case but more often than you would think.

Reference Materials:

The building inspector shall observe: Interior water supply and distribution system, including: piping materials, supports, and insulation; fixtures and faucets; functional flow; leaks; and cross connections; Interior drain, waste, and vent system, including: traps; drain, waste, and vent piping; piping supports and pipe insulation; leaks; and functional drainage; Hot water systems including: water heating equipment; normal operating controls; automatic safety controls; and chimneys, flues, and vents; Fuel storage and distribution systems including: interior fuel storage equipment, supply piping, venting, and supports; leaks; and Sump pumps. The building inspector shall describe: Water supply and distribution piping materials; Drain, waste, and vent piping materials; Water heating equipment; and Location of main water supply shutoff device. The building inspector shall operate all plumbing fixtures, including their faucets and all exterior faucets attached to the house, except where the flow end of the faucet is connected to an appliance.

The building inspector is not required to: State the effectiveness of anti-siphon devices; Determine whether water supply and waste disposal systems are public or private; Operate automatic safety controls; Operate any valve except water closet flush valves, fixture faucets, and hose faucets; Observe: Water conditioning systems; Fire and lawn sprinkler systems; On-site water supply quantity and quality; On-site waste disposal systems; Foundation irrigation systems; Spas, except as to functional flow and functional drainage; Swimming pools; Solar water heating equipment; or Observe the system for proper sizing, design, or use of proper materials.

II-B87F984D-780B-4111-ABBA-AA716FB95889.title: DOORS (Exterior)
II-B87F984D-780B-4111-ABBA-AA716FB95889.helpHtml:
Quick Check:

1. Is there any staining or discoloration that warrants a finger pressure test on exterior door trim /jambs at bottom (including sliding glass doors, patio doors, side lights etc.)?

2. Note if the main entry doors are hollow core which is not as secure as a solid core.

3. Does the garage door opening height and width seem normal?

4. The garage door must reverse when met with resistance regardless of whether or not they have sensors. Sensors should be no higher off the floor than 6" or according to manufacturer specs.

5. What is the condition of the weather-stripping at garage door floor and sides?

6. Check both sides of Garage door for damage?

7. The "jerk and let go" test for the garage door works best but there is a risk of damaging the door if you don't let go quick enough. A 2 x 4 block placed on floor can damage a metal door if door does not reverse (not recommended).

8. Note older garage door springs that do not have retention cables to contain the spring if the cable breaks.

More Info:

  1. Always open and shut a door from both sides and note whether or not the door latches.
  2. Also note if the door is out of square enough that it no longer ensures privacy.
  3. Check for holes in doors and for a doorstop on each one. Note any trim or hardware missing (check all doors).
  4. Basement or Crawlspace: Make sure that the door fits properly and is properly painted. Look at the ground in front of the door for negative slope that may allow water intrusion.
  5. Check to see if the door is delaminating or deteriorated at the bottom .
  6. Sliding glass and patio doors: Open and close doors as needed and check for "daylight" and continuous weather-stripping.
  7. Also, close the door with knob until it latches. Then turn deadbolt and check strike for proper alignment and a tight fit.
  8. Also look carefully at the glass, and check for "Cloudy" appearance or cracked glass. This is a good time to inspect the floor area around door for possible water intrusion or deterioration.
  9. Garage doors: Raise the garage door and lay a 2 x 4 block on the floor at the middle of the door opening (except a metal door that could be damaged by a 2 x 4 block). Document if the door reverses or not.
  10. If you use your hand to provide resistance and the door does not reverse, you can severely damage the door if you're not careful. The door can "fold-up" damaging the door panel and chain drive.
  11. Even if the door has electronic sensors, it still should reverse when met with resistance. Adjustment screws are usually found on the side and rear of opener. These door adjustment screws can be tricky to adjust.

Reference Materials:

II-BB8B0B61-E0C0-4BDF-B3FD-E27F113597AC.title: DOORS (Interior)
II-BB8B0B61-E0C0-4BDF-B3FD-E27F113597AC.helpHtml:
Quick Check:

1. Found mostly in bathrooms...Does the door open against a wall mounted heater that can cause a fire hazard?

2. Are doorstops or hingestops present?

3. Do doors close and latch properly?

4. Check the closet bi-fold door hardware and note whether or not the doors operate properly

More Info:

  1. All doors should latch when closed and note if the jamb rubs, because seasonal change may make the door swell and have difficulty closing.
  2. Note missing hardware, doorstop, damage etc.
  3. Check bi-folds at the top hardware location for damage.
  4. It is common for bi-folds to need adjustment. Failing to note this can sometimes create a phone call from the buyer, complaining about the bi-fold doors. Sometimes the opening for a bi-fold door needs adjustment which could be significant cosmetic work to correct the opening.

Reference Materials:

II-BD018FB9-2839-4420-8213-0362A4446CE0.title: VENTING SYSTEMS (Kitchens, baths and laundry)
II-BD018FB9-2839-4420-8213-0362A4446CE0.helpHtml:
Quick Check:

1. Do you see where the dryer vent terminates outside?

2. The clothes dryer must vent to outside air. Note if there is a lint trap kit installed instead of venting to the outside air.

3. A gas powered dryer should not use a vinyl ventpipe.

4. A bathroom needs a window or a vent fan.

More Info:

  1. Almost everyone expects an electric 220-volt connection for the Dryer.
  2. Make a note if the only connection for dryer is gas.
  3. Note if both are available, as a plus.
  4. Try to inspect the vent pipe for exhaust fans in the attic to see if they terminate outside.

Quick Check:

1. Is the heat pump / condenser level?

2. Are the foam sleeves on the suction line intact?

3. Are bushes or a fence obstructing air flow?

Distribution systems including: Fans, pumps, ducts and piping, with associated supports, dampers, insulation, air filters, registers, fan-coil units; and The presence of an installed cooling source in each room. Ambient air test is when you stick two meat thermometers into the main plenum of the air handler. One in the return air and one in the supply. Preferably near each other at the main trunk. If the AC has been running for an adequate amount of time before test you should see a range somewhere between 14 and 22 degrees. The supply should be the colder of the two. This test is not conclusive because of varying conditions but if it's out of range and the AC has had time to cool the home, then you can recommend an HVAC person (Heating Ventilation and Air Conditioning)

II-BF992F0A-4497-4043-865E-F57A5B0F7808.title: DECKS, BALCONIES, STOOPS, STEPS, AREAWAYS,  PORCHES AND APPLICABLE RAILINGS
II-BF992F0A-4497-4043-865E-F57A5B0F7808.helpHtml: Inspect slowly paying attention to ceiling, walls, floors and supports. Inspect column(s) 360 degrees for deterioration. Move away any bush that may be hiding trapped moisture. Newly painted areas on wood should be checked with finger pressure at suspicious areas. Check to see if rails are secure.

II-BF9A4075-DF32-4AFC-9263-5DCEB30272D0.title: GARAGE WALLS (INCLUDING FIREWALL SEPARATION)
II-BF9A4075-DF32-4AFC-9263-5DCEB30272D0.helpHtml:

1. Check for firewall separation when the garage wall is integral with the home's wall or another unit/condo.

2. Do you have a clear view to inspect all areas in the Garage?

3. Check the garage wall for vehicle damage or material knocked loose at the soleplate.

4. Look for bowed paneling which would be typical of a room with higher moisture levels than the rest of home.

More Info:

  1. Black flash marks on or around an outlet on the wall should be noted.
  2. Understand the difficulties of removing old wall paper.

II-C63B30E5-9E6E-4D67-A55F-51CA66B24434.title: ROOF DRAINAGE SYSTEMS
II-C63B30E5-9E6E-4D67-A55F-51CA66B24434.helpHtml:
Quick Check:

1. Note any old downspout drain tile/ piping that may no longer work properly or downspouts that need drainlines or splashblocks.

2. Look for where gutters are draining to and if there is standing water in the vicinity. Are there gutter screens installed? Are there leak signs at the gutter seams?

More Info:

  1. Be sure and comment on any negative slope towards home that may cause problems like erosion, water intrusion and silt travel.
  2. Recommend landscaping or ground cover, vegetation or a retaining wall.
  3. Sometimes a swale, trench or burm created between a dirt bank and the house (or above dirt bank) may help in diverting water.
  4. Sometimes a loose or sagging gutter is because long gutter nails have splintered through fascia and missed the rafter tail, or the rafter tail or fascia is deteriorated.
  5. I have recommended in a report that "gutters are loose and needs securing" only to get a call back saying that the rafter tails were deteriorated. While it is impossible for the inspector to check for that without repairing the loose gutter, the buyer should be made aware of the possibility that the gutters are loose because of possible deterioration. It could be as simple as some nails need replacing.

Reference Materials:

II-C897F6B7-5E8C-4A84-8B93-B1F88BB4F4A5.title: ELECTRICAL CONNECTED DEVICES AND FIXTURES
II-C897F6B7-5E8C-4A84-8B93-B1F88BB4F4A5.helpHtml:
Quick Check:

1. Is the refrigerator outlet 3 prong plug grounded?

(Baths)
2. Is there a duplex grounded outlet? If not recommend a GFCI when electrical contractor corrects.

3. The light fixture outlet in the bath should be disabled if not grounded.

4. There should be at least two outlets in each room.

5. Note any ceiling fans that wobble more than expected

6. Are there any electric outlets located on the wall above the electric baseboard, which is a possible fire hazard?

More Info:

  1. The inspection item CONNECTED DEVICES AND FIXTURES is for miscellaneous electrical items found around the property. (i.e. loose splices, boxes missing cover plates etc).
  2. I use a simple three-prong plug with a GFCI test button. It identifies whether or not the outlet is grounded, and if the polarity is correct.
  3. Some tips are: Your three-prong GFCI test plug will not "trip" the outlet if it is a non-grounded GFCI. It should still trip by pressing the test button on the outlet, and kill the circuit.
  4. A non-grounded outlet can be corrected by either attaching a ground wire to the outlet and attach it to a metal rod or a metal plumbing pipe.
  5. Or, replace the three-prongnon-grounded outlet with a three-prong GFCI outlet. A sticker should be on the outlet that identifies it as non-grounded.
  6. Or last, change the circuit breaker to a GFCI breaker at panel.
  7. You can "trip" a non-grounded GFCI with a voltmeter by placing one prong of the voltmeter in the short slit of the outlet, and take the other prong of the voltmeter and touch a metal plumbing pipe (that eventually contacts the soil).
  8. Most three-prong GFCI plugs will show two lights at the end of the plug when the outlet being tested is grounded. When you press the button on the plug, both lights should remain lit and strong. If however, the plug lights up only one of the two grounding lights "Faint or Dim" and you press the button on the plug and it shows "Reverse polarity", it may just be a "loose" ground wire and can be corrected a lot easier than having to install a new ground wire.
  9. Just because you can press the test button on the GFCI outlet using your finger and it "trips," doesn't mean it killed the circuit. It could be defective.
  10. New GFCI outlets that are installed can be defective.
  11. Always use the three-prong GFCI test plug on every three-prong outlet.
  12. Homeowners frequently use a freezer in their garage. Most outlets in the garage are on a GFCI Circuit. When you're inspecting the home, don't forget to reset the GFCI outlet or you may be buying the homeowners spoiled food.

II-C91DD79E-7152-464C-91B1-31CD1D2EDBBB.title: ROOF COVERINGS
II-C91DD79E-7152-464C-91B1-31CD1D2EDBBB.helpHtml:
Quick Check:

1. Are there any noticeable sways or sags in the roof?

2. Do you estimate the life remaining on the roof covering to be 5 years or less?

3. Are there any repair signs on the roof?

4. Are there any sides or areas of the roof that were not inspected due to noaccess?

More Info:

  1. I don't get up on all roofs, but many if not most of the roofs I see are accessible. These are walkable roofs and not too steep.
  2. Hair-line cracks that sometimes occur on shingles cannot be seen unless you go up on the roof. Caulking or repair signs can be missed as well. If you're on the roof, look for boot flange for vent pipes to see if they fit the pipe to keep out rain.
  3. I don't walk on tile roofs or wood shakes for fear of damaging them or falling.
  4. Never step out on a metal awning.

Reference Materials:

The home inspector shall observe: Roof covering; Roof drainage systems; Flashings; Skylights, chimneys, and roof penetrations; and signs of' leaks or abnormal condensation on building components. The home inspector shall: Describe the type of roof covering materials; and Report the methods used to observe the roofing.

The home inspector is not required to: Walk on the roofing; or Observe attached accessories including but not limited to solar systems, antennae, and lightning arrestors.

II-C9B122A9-8D3E-4C5F-87BE-81361C27F929.title: RANGES/OVENS/COOKTOPS
II-C9B122A9-8D3E-4C5F-87BE-81361C27F929.helpHtml:
Quick Check:

1. Are the support clips in place for the baking or broiler elements in the oven?

2. Are the control knobs legible on the range and do they work properly?

3. Are the grease filters in place and clean for the range fan?

More Info:

  1. First, turn on the broiler in the oven while touching the element, turn off and check the bake element.
  2. Then check the support clips that hold the broiler and bake elements in place, to make sure they're not missing or loose.
  3. Check the oven door for warping and inspect the gasket seal.
  4. Check for burn marks on the oven door frame and for heat loss from a failed gasket and door alignment and springs.
  5. Open and close the storage drawer and check for proper operation.
  6. Turn on all the burners to high, turn back off and finger touch. This method works, and you don't have the risk of someone in the home getting burned while elements are cooling down from the high setting.
  7. On Gas stoves check all burners for even flame at all settings.
  8. Recommend cleaning if a burner delays ignition or if flames pop or if they are uneven.

Reference Materials:

II-CE563563-028F-42C0-8F59-5564E1D424C3.title: COUNTERS AND A REPRESENTATIVE NUMBER OF CABINETS
II-CE563563-028F-42C0-8F59-5564E1D424C3.helpHtml:
Quick Check:

1. Check the countertop at sink rim for absorption or damage.

2. Check the backside of drawers at the cabinet base for mold.

3. Check the wall behind the refrigerator for mold.

4. Check the Icemaker line behind the refrigerator for kinks or damage.

5. Are there any extra large cut-outs for plumbing or the range vent that may allow air infiltration from the attic or crawlspace?

6. What is the microwave clearance from the range?

7. Is the sink base deteriorated or sagging from previous leaks at the bottom shelf?

8. Does the back splash on the counter behind the sink prevent splash water from possibly going behind sink base and causing mold on concealed wall?

9. Is the kick board missing anywhere in the kitchen cabinetry that may allow trash to collect or rodents to enter?

10. Is the wall cabinetry secure?

11. Is the shelving warped?

12. Make sure the island cabinet cannot be moved if a wired outlet is present

More Info:

  1. For new building construction, it is important to look for workmanship flaws in installation and mounting of cabinets or securing the countertop.
  2. Cabinets are expensive and you should be aware of high expectations from your client on having near perfect workmanship and installations of crown, trim, joining sides of two cabinets, cut-out for the dishwasher and cut-outs for the plumbing lines the size of a baseball.
  3. Islands that are moveable but have a wired outlet, should be noted as well.
  4. The dishwasher needs to be secured under the counter.
  5. Tile counters should not be sharp or have the cut edge exposed along the counter edge (sharp).
  6. Make sure counters that overhang or extend towards a range top are not to close to the rear burner or heating element because of a fire hazard.
  7. Remember, in new construction, there are no excuses for less than near perfect cabinet installation.

Reference Materials:

II-D1900C54-47FA-438B-B819-C311388425C4.title: HOT WATER SYSTEMS, CONTROLS, CHIMNEYS, FLUES AND VENTS
II-D1900C54-47FA-438B-B819-C311388425C4.helpHtml:
Quick Check:

1. Is the gas water heater 18" off the floor and mounted on a proper stand or support?

2. Is the water heater strapped securely to the wall (required in earthquake zones)?

3. If the gas line to the water heater or furnace could be bumped or ruptured by a vehicle, a pole or guard post should be recommended

4. If the water heater is in the crawlspace or basement, it should not be lower than ground level. You may not dig a hole to set the water heater in.

5. Use a lighter at the draft hood when the gas water heater is on to check for proper draw.

6. A gas water heater in the closet needs fresh air from the attic at the ceiling and near the floor.

More Info:

  1. Inspect the plumbing connections and tank housing.
  2. Note rust signs from moisture or condensation (if in a damp area of home) or possible leak at the liner.
  3. Rust along the bottom can be caused when water leaks out while changing heating elements. Sometimes it's hard to distinguish. If you discover rust along the bottom, then remove panel access and feel the insulation to determine if it's currently wet.
  4. Water heaters installed in a crawlspace should not be below ground level.
  5. Gas water heaters installed in a garage should be at least 18 inches off the ground.
  6. When two gas vent pipes enter the chimney together, the highest BTU should enter chimney under the smaller BTU.
  7. Gas water heaters should have the thermostat turned up to force it to come on in order to test the draw at the diverter with a match or lighter. If the draw does not noticeably suck in flame on a match, there could be a venting problem.
  8. White deposits and rust on metal vent pipe can occur from moisture in the gas when not venting properly.
  9. A greasy residue on top of the gas water heater is also a sign of a vent problem.
  10. A blackened or smoky appearance on and around the housing near the flame of a gas water heater indicates the need for more air (combustion air).
  11. The T&P valve (Test and Pressure or Pop off valve) can look fine if the home has not had the water heater on 24 hours before inspection. It can then leak after the buyer moves in. The primary reason is that pressure on the system builds up at night when no one is using water. With gas, the added pressure is a result of steam. Be aware of this when you inspect a vacant home and the water heater has not been on for 24 hours prior.

Reference Materials:

II-D1DBCBB2-A794-4E3D-BF61-CFB0DC603255.title: DOORS (Interior and Exterior)
II-D1DBCBB2-A794-4E3D-BF61-CFB0DC603255.helpHtml: Always open and shut a door from both sides and note whether or not the door latches. Also note if the door is out of square enough that it no longer ensures privacy. Check for holes in the door and for a doorstop. Note any trim missing, or hardware (check all doors). BASEMENT/CRAWLSPACE: Make sure that the door fits properly and is properly painted. Look at the ground in front of the door for negative slope that may allow water intrusion. Always check the basement or crawlspace last (after you run water at all fixtures inside) to find leaks. When you do enter crawl space, look at each inside wall, left and right of entry, for water or mud marks on wall. If the basement entry is below grade with steps, check to see if a floor drain exists and that it appears to work properly. Check to see if the door is delaminating on the bottom or deteriorated. SLIDING GLASS DOORS AND PATIO DOORS:  Open and close the door as needed and check for "Day light" and continuous weather-stripping. Also close the door with the knob until it latches. Then turn the deadbolt and check strike for proper alignment and a tight fit. Also look carefully at the glass, and check for "Cloudy" appearance or cracked glass. This is a good time to inspect the floor area around door for possible water intrusion or deterioration. GARAGE DOORS: Raise the garage door and lay a 2 x 4 block on the floor at the middle of the door opening. Document if the door reverses or not. If you use your hand to resist, and the door does not reverse, you can severely damage the door if not careful. The door can "fold-up", damaging the door panel and chain drive. Even if the door has electronic sensors it still should reverse when met with resistance. Adjustment screws are usually found on the side and rear of the opener.

II-D57D862A-2A23-4CBA-9C18-DAB93EC1F68D.title: WATER HEATER EQUIPMENT
II-D57D862A-2A23-4CBA-9C18-DAB93EC1F68D.helpHtml: Inspect the plumbing connections and tank housing. Note rust signs from moisture or condensation (if in a damp area of home) or possible leak at liner. Rust along bottom can be caused when water leaks out while changing heat elements. Sometimes it's hard to distinguish. If you discover rust along bottom, then remove panel access and feel the insulation to determine if it's currently wet. Water heaters installed in a crawlspace should not be below ground level. Gas water heaters installed in a garage should be at least 18 inches off the ground. When two gas vent pipes enter the chimney together, the highest BTU should enter chimney under the smaller BTU. See Discoveries and Auto Comments. Gas water heaters should be cranked up to come on and test draw at diverter with a match. If draw does not suck out flame on match, there could be a venting problem. White deposits and rust on metal vent pipe can occur from moisture in gas when not venting properly. A greasy residue on top of gas water heater is also a sign of a vent problem.

II-D6D2686A-2766-453D-818A-0673201ECDD8.title: PRESENCE OF INSTALLED COOLING SOURCE IN EACH ROOM
II-D6D2686A-2766-453D-818A-0673201ECDD8.helpHtml:
Quick Check:

More Info:

  1. Don't miss the absence of a vent in a room or you could be sued and be liable for the cost to put one in.
  2. One must also consider: Why isn't one there? It could be the size of the heat/AC unit which would require a bigger unit or perhaps there is no physical way to install one. Extreme remodeling may be involved.
  3. Also, stay alert for the type of heating system in the house with an AC condenser. If it's boiler heat and there is an AC unit outside, and the house is 2 story, it is likely that the AC serves the upstairs only. Therefore it is necessary to point this out in your report.

II-D830F437-0CB7-4B0A-A585-D9116A58E890.title: FUEL STORAGE AND DISTRIBUTION SYSTEMS (Interior fuel storage, piping, venting, supports, leaks)
II-D830F437-0CB7-4B0A-A585-D9116A58E890.helpHtml:
Quick Check:

1. Is the oil barrel or propane tank leaning, leaking, or too small for the home?

2. Is the oil barrel stand leaning or weak? Are there stains on the ground from oil drips?

3. Are the oil or gas fuel lines damaged or kinked?

4. Does the Gas Dryer have a shut-off valve above the floor?

5. The Natural Gas lineshould not be soft copper until it comes through the floor or walls

More Info:

  1. Always tell the client when you discover an oil barrel in the ground.
  2. Always tell them that you did not test the soil for possible contamination or if the oil barrel is leaking or not.
  3. Always make sure that gas piping has a cap on any unused end.
  4. Soft copper piping for gas is not allowed in my area unless it is propane. This is when the piping travels through floors or walls etc. and can only change to soft piping like copper above the floor. A shut-off valve above the floor is required.

Reference Materials:

II-D8A1C918-C020-4AEC-A553-5B7466F09997.title: NORMAL OPERATING CONTROLS
II-D8A1C918-C020-4AEC-A553-5B7466F09997.helpHtml:
Quick Check:

Check the thermostat for damage or operation. See if the kill switch on air handler works.

More Info:

II-D8CDD9A3-3AA7-4567-B961-7CD451A72220.title: GARAGE DOOR (S)
II-D8CDD9A3-3AA7-4567-B961-7CD451A72220.helpHtml:
Quick Check:

1. Is there any staining or discoloration that warrants a finger pressure test on exterior door trim /jambs at bottom ?

2. Does the garage door opening height and width seem normal?

3. The garage door must reverse when met with resistance regardless of whether or not they have sensors. Sensors should be no higher off the floor than 6" or according to manufacturer specs.

4. What is the condition of the weather-stripping at garage door floor and sides?

5. Check both sides of Garage door for damage?

6. The "jerk and let go" test for the garage door works best but there is a risk of damaging the door if you don't let go quick enough. A 2 x 4 block placed on floor can damage a metal door if door does not reverse (not recommended).

8. Note older garage door springs that do not have retention cables to contain the spring if the cable breaks.

More Info:

  1. Always open and shut a door from both sides and note whether or not the door latches.
  2. Also note if the door is out of square enough that it no longer ensures privacy.
  3. Check for holes in doors and for a doorstop on each one. Note any trim or hardware missing (check all doors).
  4. Basement or Crawlspace: Make sure that the door fits properly and is properly painted. Look at the ground in front of the door for negative slope that may allow water intrusion.
  5. Check to see if the door is delaminating or deteriorated at the bottom .
  6. Sliding glass and patio doors: Open and close doors as needed and check for "daylight" and continuous weather-stripping.
  7. Also, close the door with knob until it latches. Then turn deadbolt and check strike for proper alignment and a tight fit.
  8. Also look carefully at the glass, and check for "Cloudy" appearance or cracked glass. This is a good time to inspect the floor area around door for possible water intrusion or deterioration.
  9. Garage doors: Raise the garage door and lay a 2 x 4 block on the floor at the middle of the door opening (except a metal door that could be damaged by a 2 x 4 block). Document if the door reverses or not.
  10. If you use your hand to provide resistance and the door does not reverse, you can severely damage the door if you're not careful. The door can "fold-up" damaging the door panel and chain drive.
  11. Even if the door has electronic sensors, it still should reverse when met with resistance. Adjustment screws are usually found on the side and rear of opener. These door adjustment screws can be tricky to adjust.

II-D94A2304-9E4C-4847-B664-122A5613F028.title: BATHROOM EXHAUST FANS AND/OR HEATERS
II-D94A2304-9E4C-4847-B664-122A5613F028.helpHtml: Check for operation. check in all modes (i.e. heat/fan/light) if applicable. Note if noisy or overwattage of bulb. Try to check for venting to the outside (in attic).

II-DA4B4DD5-58CD-4DCD-9FAE-7809D18431C7.title: GAS/LP FIRELOGS AND FIREPLACES
II-DA4B4DD5-58CD-4DCD-9FAE-7809D18431C7.helpHtml:
Quick Check:

1. Verify if using gas or propane logs by ID plate. A fork shaped flame nozzle usually means vented and a straw shaped nozzle usually means non-vented.

2. (Newer Construction)Make sure that the type of gas logs match the fuel type for the home (i.e. Gas logs for natural gas and propane logs for propane gas).

3. Visually examine fire logs for damage.

4. Black soot build up on logs usually means incorrect placement or arrangement. Refer to Manual specifications.

5. Note if the damper is missing or if the lid does not shut off air completely

More Info:

  1. Non-vented firelogs are not allowed in sleeping rooms.
  2. Always mention this in your report when small coal Fireplace(s) are present.
  3. A lot of Buyers will try to convert old coal FP to gas logs and need to know about venting requirements.
  4. Check the metal ID tag and make sure that the type of fuel at the house matches the type that the logs are designed for (Gas or LP).

Reference Materials:

II-DA53B7CB-44E7-4FD3-B91E-387FDDFD4F4E.title: INSULATION UNDER FLOOR SYSTEM
II-DA53B7CB-44E7-4FD3-B91E-387FDDFD4F4E.helpHtml:
Quick Check:

1. Is insulation right side up? (Paper side faces the heated space).

2. Is there any loose, missing or hanging insulation?

More Info:

  1. To get R-Value for Fiberglass, Rock Wool and Mineral Fiber, multiply the thickness in inches by 3.142857.
  2. For Cellulose, multiply inches by 3.6666 to find R-Value.
  3. Insulation usually comes in four types: Loose-fill, Batts, Rolls and Rigid Foam Board.
  4. Fiberglass is recycled glass and sand
  5. Rock Wool is recycled Steel scraps and Basaltic Rock
  6. Cellulose is recycled newspapers treated with fire retardant chemicals (Borax).
  7. Rigid Foam Board (used on exterior side of walls and behind the ceiling panel of a Cathedral ceiling) obviously not visible or accessible during an inspection.
  8. A home can lose 50% of it's heat through the roof, with 25% going through the walls and windows, and 25% through the floor.

A rough guess of R value in the attic is determined by the thickness of insulation:

  1. about 6 inches thick or just under 22 R value
  2. about 7 inches thick or 25.6 R-value
  3. about 8 inches thick or just over 29 R-value
  4. about 9 inches thick or just under 33 R-value
  5. about 10 inches thick or just over 36.6 R-value
  6. about 11 inches thick or just over 40 R-value
  7. about 12 inches thick or just under 44 R-value
  8. about 13 inches thick or 47.6 R-value
  9. about 14 inches thick or just at 51 R-value
  10. about 15 inches thick or just under 55 R-value
  11. about 16 inches thick or 58 R-value

Reference Materials:

The home inspector shall observe: Insulation and vapor retarders in unfinished spaces; Ventilation of attics and foundation areas; Kitchen, bathroom, and laundry venting systems; and the operation of any readily accessible attic ventilation fan, and, when temperature permits, the operation of any readily accessible thermostatic control. The home inspector shall describe: Insulation in unfinished spaces; and Absence of insulation in unfinished space at conditioned surfaces. The home inspector shall: Move insulation where readily visible evidence indicates the need to do so; and Move insulation where chimneys penetrate roofs, where plumbing drain/waste pipes penetrate floors, adjacent to earth filled stoops or porches, and at exterior doors.

The home inspector is not required to report on: Concealed insulation and vapor retarders; or Venting equipment that is integral with household appliances.

II-DAF34BA1-AD26-49A1-BBA6-56CAC477BED1.title: SKYLIGHTS, CHIMNEYS AND ROOF PENETRATIONS
II-DAF34BA1-AD26-49A1-BBA6-56CAC477BED1.helpHtml:
Quick Check:

1. Does the vent pipe boot/flange on roof fit snug around the pipe?

2. Inspect the chimney above the roofline for Spalling, cracks, missing mortar or missing rain cap.

3. Inspect the chimney crown and note any cracked or missing mortar, or improper caulking or silicone in cracks that may fail.

4. Do ridge vents have end caps and nail heads caulked? Are passive vents flashed properly? Do turbines turn freely?

5. Does the skylight have a flash kit or was it homemade? Are there repair/caulk signs? Cloudy appearance?

6. Is chimney leaning or are there signs of trim rework where chimney contacts the wall of building?

More Info:

  1. Skylights without manufactured flash kits can leak a lot easier than properly installed flash kits.
  2. Skylights can go for years with no problems and leak only after time has passed and for no apparent reason noticed.
  3. Skylights can leak on one rainy day and not leak on another. It is impossible to look at a skylight installation and know if it will leak or not. Even when it looks perfect.
  4. Homes that have had a pressure washing company spray onto skylights can blow away, or push sealant caulking away, and cause leaks. You can't know what has happened since the skylight has been installed.
  5. Look for fresh paint inside at the skylight chase or tell-tale water marks that may only be condensation and not leaks.
  6. Vaulted ceilings with skylights can cause condensation in summer, if the ceiling air gets hot enough and an AC vent is mixing with hot ceiling air. Water droplets (or stains) can form on the ceiling. Sometimes it is difficult to determine which one is occurring in the building.
  7. Chimneys: Look for loose mortar above the roof line.
  8. Check the cement crown for cracks.
  9. White efflorescence or flaking of brick (spalling) indicates moisture is soaking into the brick somewhere.
  10. Do not try to remove metal hood bonnets on chimney to inspect liner. They sometimes are difficult to get back on or have been semi-permanently glued requiring a lot of work each time it is removed.
  11. Wood siding chimneys can deteriorate if metal hood does not completely cover outside corner boards.
  12. Stucco peeling away from the surface it is bonded to, is generally caused from moisture or a previously painted sub surface (painted masonry block that stucco is applied on).
  13. Brick divider walls separating flues are still found on many old homes. Loose or missing brick in these divider walls calls for a certified chimney sweep to inspect further.
  14. Roof penetrations: Know how to flash a chimney, install a vent pipe or vent fan hood flange into the weave of shingles.
